authority: docs/tier3/agent-definition-standard.md (schema) and docs/tier7/ticket-43-role-bindings-decision.md (the decisions). Protected by policy/ in protected-paths.json; a change here is a requalification event.
notes: A binding turns a palette kind — a role, and per the glossary never a valid agent definition — into a capability: (input contract, output contract, tools, permissions, criteria, escalation).

capability_id IS the routing key. policy/model-routing.json maps it to a model. Ticket #43 D5 gave the binding a separate `model` reference field; ticket #46 D4 then made capability_id itself the key, so that field would be a second name for one join and is deliberately absent.
The version fields below are the fingerprint's D19 group. Editing one is a requalification event: it changes the fingerprint, and the glossary suspends every autonomy grant on a fingerprint change.

bindable is stated explicitly rather than derived from category. Deriving it breaks silently when a non-agent kind is added outside the operator category; the lint cross-checks the two and fails on disagreement.

bindable_values.agent: dispatched to a runtime agent; carries a full binding record
bindable_values.unbound: a legitimate palette kind that no lifecycle phase dispatches today
bindable_values.never: may never be delegated to an agent — the operator kinds, and anything else a human must hold

bindings.unbound_reason: No ECC agent performs requirements interrogation. ECC's 68 agents are language reviewers and build resolvers; `council` is a skill, not an agent. This kind runs Alfred-native until an agent exists for it, and the empty list says so rather than binding a near-miss.

bindings.independence: santa-method — two agents, both must pass, and neither may be the agent that ran Execute

bindings.unbound_reason: No ECC agent may hold validation authority. `verification-loop` and `eval-harness` are skills, not agents, and `agent-evaluator` is classified never authoritative — an agent rating its own output is a self-reported verdict from the executing session. Validation runs Alfred-native, against the criterion, outside the agent tree.
